text:
sam_support: Hey @michael_customer — sorry you're hitting that auth + latency problem. To help us reproduce the fastest, can you share ONE request id (or two) plus either a HAR or a minimal curl reproducer? Below are short, copy-paste steps depending on where you're calling from.

sam_support: Quick checklist we need:
- 1x request id (from console or SDK logs)
- Screenshot of the error in Console (if you used the Console)
- HAR file or curl that reproduces the issue (ideally <100KB)
- Your client version / SDK version and region (us-west-2, etc.)
- Approx timestamp (UTC) when you saw the bad request

sam_support: Console (web) -> Request id
- Open Redwood Console -> Observability -> Requests (or the request row).
- Click the request; the Request ID is shown at the top of the detail pane as `Request ID:` — copy that string.
- There's also a "Copy debug bundle" button in the top-right if available; that bundles logs + HAR.

sam_support: Chrome HAR capture (browser)
1. Open DevTools -> Network tab
2. Reproduce the request, right-click the network table -> Save all as HAR with content
3. Attach the .har file (rename to something like `michael-2026-02-10.har`)

sam_support: Minimal curl repro (examples)
```bash
# standard generation request (replace <REQ_ID> and <API_KEY>)
curl -i -X POST 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -H "X-Request-ID: <REQ_ID>" 
  --data '{"model":"gpt-4o-instruct","input":"hello"}' 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

sam_support: SDKs / mobile
- iOS (SDK >=0.9): call `RedwoodSDK.lastRequestId()` in logs or use debug menu -> "Copy last request id".
- Android: check logcat for `x-rw-request-id` header or call `Redwood.getLastRequestId()` if using the helper.
- If you can't get the id, send the client timestamp + approximate local time and we can look up nearby requests.

michael_customer: Thanks — I found two ids: `req_20260210_abc123` and `req_20260210_def456`. Uploaded a HAR called `michael_session_2026-02-10.har`. Screenshot also attached.

jess_eng: @sam_support can you also ask for the exact request payload and the SDK version? For latency issues we need sequence length and whether KV cache was used.

sam_support: Good call. @michael_customer can you paste the minimal request payload you used (just model, input length, temperature, filters) and the sdk/client version (e.g., redwood-js 1.4.2)? Example: 
```json
{"model":"gpt-4o-instruct","input":"<trimmed prompt>","max_tokens":512}
```

michael_customer: Payload was basically the example: `{"model":"gpt-4o-instruct","input":"Summarize...","max_tokens":256}`. Using redwood-ios 0.9.1. Region: us-east-1. Time approx: 2026-02-10T18:23:05Z.

sam_support: Perfect — this is good. One more quick ask: can you redact any PII in the HAR but keep headers intact (we need `Authorization` removed but leave `X-Request-ID` / `x-rw-request-id` if present).

michael_customer: Done — removed auth header, uploaded `michael_session_2026-02-10_redacted.har` and put the two request ids in the ticket. Also pasted a curl repro below: 
```bash
curl -i -X POST 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" 
  -H "X-Request-ID: req_20260210_abc123" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  --data '{"model":"gpt-4o-instruct","input":"Summarize the following...","max_tokens":256}' 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

infra-bot: Debug bundle created: https://console.redwood.ai/debug/DB-9a7b (contains server traces + attached HAR)

oncall_maya: I grabbed the two request IDs and started a trace lookup — seeing a 502 gateway at the same minute for one of them, will dig into kernel timeouts and upstream. Assigning to eng: @jess_eng.

jess_eng: Thanks, will check the runtime logs and whether the request hit a fallback model. If we need more data we'll ask for the full console debug token but the HAR + ids are great to start.

sam_support: Thanks @michael_customer — we'll follow up in this thread once we have a root cause. Appreciate the quick repro materials :thumbsup:
